messages:
Mike L: Heads up — ran `terraform plan` in the staging workspace and it wants to recreate a bunch of k8s RoleBinding resources (e.g. default/ci-runner). I didn't touch RBAC. Anyone else seeing weird recreates after the provider bump?

Anya P: I noticed similar yesterday after we bumped the kubernetes provider. Did you run `terraform init -upgrade` in that workspace?

Mike L: yes, we upgraded from 2.16.0 -> 2.17.0 and reinitialized. The plan shows provider address drift in the diff (provider address in state vs code). Example in plan:
```
~ resource "kubernetes_role_binding" "ci_runner" {
    provider = registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes
  }

- provider = registry.terraform.io/-/kubernetes
+ provider = registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes
```

Kevin: that looks like the canonical provider address changed (old anonymous source -> explicit hashicorp source). Terraform can treat that as needing to recreate unless the state provider meta is updated. Quick check: `terraform state show <resource>` and look for `provider` metadata.

Mike L: here's what `terraform state show` prints for one of the resources:
```
# kubernetes_role_binding.ci_runner:
resource "kubernetes_role_binding" "ci_runner" {
  id = "default/ci-runner"
  metadata {
    name = "ci-runner"
    namespace = "default"
  }
  subjects = [ ... ]
  role_ref = { ... }
  # provider = registry.terraform.io/-/kubernetes
}
```

Sarah: yep that's the problem — state still references the old provider address. Two non-destructive options: 1) use `terraform state replace-provider` to update provider addresses in state, or 2) import the resource under the new provider address (pain). Prefer #1. Example command: 
```
terraform state replace-provider \
  'registry.terraform.io/-/kubernetes' \
  'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes' 
```
Run that against the staging workspace (make a backup first). It rewrites provider refs in state without touching resources.

Kevin: also double-check your CLI and Terraform version combos — `state replace-provider` was added in 1.1 I think. If you don't have it, fallback is `terraform state pull` edit the JSON (ugh) and `terraform state push` or run a targeted `terraform import` per resource.

Mike L: good call. We are on Terraform 1.5.3 so command exists. Any concerns about drift after replace?

Anya P: after replace, run `terraform plan` with `-refresh=true` and verify only the provider meta changed. If anything else shows up, post the diff. Also try on a copy of state or run from a maintainer session.

infra-oncall-bot: locking note — staging state is currently unlocked. Last lock expired: 1769456900. If you plan a replace, avoid concurrent applies.

Sarah: one more tip: if there are provider aliased blocks in your module (alias blocks), ensure the alias names match. Mismatched alias + different source can cause Terraform to still think it's different.

Mike L: thanks — I'll run `terraform state replace-provider` on a clone of the state first and report back. If it works, I'll open a short PR documenting the provider-address change and the remediation steps so other teams don't trip on this. :thumbsup:
